section_2.title: A degree route built for adults without A-levels.
section_2.description: A Foundation year (Year 0) is a one-year preparation course attached to a full degree — the standard route into university for adults, fully funded by Student Finance England.

section_3.title: What a Foundation Year actually is.
section_3.description: The first year of a four-year integrated degree. It bridges school and university — giving you the academic skills, subject grounding and confidence to thrive on the main degree.

cards.title: No A-levels required
cards.description: The biggest barrier to university is removed. Work experience or simply being a motivated mature applicant can be enough.

cards.title: Full SFE funding from Year 0
cards.description: Funded as part of your degree — Tuition Fee Loan, Maintenance Loan and any grants you qualify for, the same as Years 1–3.

cards.title: Same university, same degree
cards.description: You progress straight into Year 1 without re-applying. Your final certificate is identical to a 3-year degree.

section_4.title: Foundation Year courses you can study.
section_4.description: Every course below offers a Year 0 entry route, accepts adults without A-levels, and is fully Student Finance eligible.

section_6.title: What certificate do I get?
section_6.description: A Foundation year is part of the full degree. What you get depends on how far you progress — exit awards exist as a safety net.

cards.title: Pass Year 0
cards.description: A Certificate of Foundation Studies — recognition of completed Level 3 study.

cards.title: + Year 1
cards.description: Exit with a Certificate of Higher Education (CertHE) — a Level 4 qualification.

cards.title: + Years 1 & 2
cards.description: Exit with a Diploma of Higher Education (DipHE) — a Level 5 qualification.

cards.title: All 4 years
cards.description: A full Bachelor's degree (BA/BSc) — identical to a 3-year degree. No “with foundation” on the certificate.

section_7.title: Can you get in — and get funded?
section_7.description: Two things decide it: whether you meet the academic entry route, and whether your residency status qualifies you for Student Finance. Here's both.

cards.title: With Level 3 qualifications
points: Any Level 3 qualification — A-levels, BTEC, Access to HE, NVQ Level 3 — usually at any grade
GCSE Maths & English at Grade 4/C (some providers accept lower with an assessment)
A personal statement explaining your motivation and goals

cards.title: Without formal qualifications
points: Substantial work experience — often 2+ years — can count in place of academic grades
No A-levels required; this is the standard adult route into university
Some courses ask for a short interview or written task instead

cards.title: Access to HE Diploma
points: A one-year Level 3 course designed for adults — widely accepted for Foundation Year entry
Often a strong route if you left school without A-levels but want structured preparation

cards.title: Common things to check first
points: No GCSEs: most universities offer a free pre-entry assessment or short equivalency
English not your first language: B1 (≈ IELTS 5.0–5.5) is the usual foundation entry minimum
Previous higher education study: SFE funding may be affected by prior study (ELQ rules)

section_9.title: Foundation Year vs Foundation Degree.
section_9.description: They sound similar but are very different — getting it wrong can waste a year of funding entitlement.

questionAnswer.question: What it is
questionAnswer.answer: The first year of a four-year integrated Bachelor's degree (1 + 3 years).

questionAnswer.question: What you get
questionAnswer.answer: A full Bachelor's degree after all 4 years — identical to a 3-year degree.

questionAnswer.question: Best for
questionAnswer.answer: Adults without A-levels who want a full Bachelor's but need preparation first.

questionAnswer.question: What it is
questionAnswer.answer: A standalone Level 5 qualification (≈ first two years of a Bachelor's). Vocational.

questionAnswer.question: What you get
questionAnswer.answer: A Foundation Degree on its own — you can then “top up” to a full Bachelor's in one extra year.

questionAnswer.question: Best for
questionAnswer.answer: People who want a work-relevant qualification with the option to top up later.

faqs.question: Does a Foundation year cost extra?
faqs.answer: It uses one year of your Student Finance entitlement, funded at the same rate as any other year. There's no upfront cost — the tuition fee loan goes directly to your university.

faqs.question: Will my degree certificate say "with foundation"?
faqs.answer: No. On completing all four years you receive a full Bachelor's degree (BA/BSc) — the certificate is identical to a 3-year degree.

faqs.question: Do I need to pass everything to progress?
faqs.answer: You need to pass the Foundation year to move into Year 1. Around 80–90% of foundation-year students progress through to graduation.

faqs.question: Can I get a Maintenance Loan during the Foundation year?
faqs.answer: Yes — the maintenance loan is available for all four years, the same as a standard degree, assessed on your household income.

faqs.question: What if I've studied at degree level before?
faqs.answer: Equivalent or Lower Qualification (ELQ) rules may affect new tuition funding. Some exceptions exist (healthcare, teaching) — check your eligibility before applying.

routes.title: HND

routes.title: Top-Up Degree
